html:
SMTO-API-0014 — API service unavailable

GUID: 177b8895-d37f-4a38-a8bc-a1bf5baa24a3
Slug: api-service-unavailable
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO, or a part it depends on, couldn't handle this request right now. It may be starting up, stopping, updating, or unreachable from where you are.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a minute, then reload the page. If SMTO is starting or updating, wait until its startup screen shows Ready. Parts of SMTO turn requests away until they have finished starting.
  2. Open System Health and look under Needs attention to see which part is not available. It shows whether SMTO itself, a Gateway or a model service is the part not responding.
  3. Before repeating anything that changes data, check whether your earlier attempt already went through. The request may have reached SMTO just before the problem started.
  4. If you saw this after an aor command in a terminal, make sure SMTO is running. For aor doctor, also check the address you gave after --server-url. The command stops when it can't reach SMTO at that address or doesn't trust SMTO's security certificate.

What success looks like

  • System Health shows the part working, and the page or command responds normally.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data or turn off certificate checks to make the error go away; that can lose work or weaken security.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The CLI could not connect to the configured Server, or an SMTO or Gateway endpoint returned HTTP 503 (for example portal setup or password storage unavailable, the Manual still preparing, or Gateway event subscriber capacity reached) with no more specific registered cause.

What this means

  • The CLI cannot connect to the configured remote endpoint, or generic HTTP enrichment reports service unavailability. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • The CLI cannot connect to the configured remote endpoint, or generic HTTP enrichment reports service unavailability.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish local connection failure from a returned service-unavailable response and inspect original dispatch state.

How to fix it

  • Check the reported dependency's health (System Health, or the Server startup report via aor doctor --server-url) and restore it before sending more work; for CLI connection failures, verify the server address, port and TLS trust. Honor any Retry-After header, and confirm the state of previously submitted work before resubmitting.
  • Inspect the required service health and restore it before requesting further work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended service route is healthy and any previously submitted work is reconciled before another request.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
